podcast.body: Bill Haley and His Comets' 1954 recording of "Rock Around the Clock" gained immense cultural significance, particularly after being featured over the opening and closing credits of the 1955 movie *Blackboard Jungle*. Initially, its release did not cause much stir, but its association with the film, especially in Britain in 1956, ignited a phenomenon of rebellious audience behavior in theaters, including dancing in aisles, seat carving, fighting, and turning firehoses on each other. This led to widespread condemnation of rock and roll music. "But the 1954 recording by Bill Haley in the comments was the one that threatened to bring down the British Empire."

podcast.body: This song was used in the opening titles of the 1955 MGM film *Blackboard Jungle*, marking the first time a rock and roll song was ever featured in a Hollywood feature film. The movie was intended to warn against juvenile delinquency, but the song's inclusion famously led to kids dancing in theaters, sometimes resulting in violence and vandalism. The film was subsequently banned in many cities and throughout the UK. "This was the first time a rock and roll song was ever used in a Hollywood feature film."
